blocks.text: 执行摘要

inlines.text: 执行摘要
Wiz Research 在 PHP 核心中发现了多个严重漏洞。PHP 是一种流行的通用脚本语言，为全球 70% 的网站提供支持。成功利用这些漏洞可能使攻击者控制受影响的服务器、窃取敏感数据，并篡改其上运行的网站。
PHP 是 Web 的支柱：它是驱动 WordPress、Joomla、Drupal、维基百科的 MediaWiki 以及许多其他项目的编程语言。
这些漏洞包括内存泄露和未经身份验证的远程代码执行，
且存在于 PHP 本身，与运行在其上的应用程序无关
，使每个受影响的网站都面临直接风险。
过去十年发布的每个 PHP 版本都至少受其中一个漏洞影响，最早可追溯至 5.4 版本。攻击者可以远程利用这些漏洞，某些情况下还相当容易。强烈建议立即打补丁。
PHP 发布了补丁
，修复了核心引擎中的多个内存安全漏洞。
这些发现属于 PHP 中发现的最严重漏洞之列，也可以说是软件史上最严重的漏洞之一。底层缺陷已存在数十年，但要证明其可利用性，需要一条异常复杂的步骤链，处于人类研究人员实际所能达到的极限边缘。前沿 AI 模型大幅降低了这一门槛，将长期存在的缺陷转化为可实际利用的漏洞。

blocks.text: 概述

inlines.text: 概述

blocks.text: 在本文中，我们解释前沿 AI 如何帮助我们找到并修复在 PHP 代码库中隐藏了十多年的漏洞。下文描述的问题均源于关键的架构决策，其中一些决策在十多年前就已做出，并被归入两个 CVE，严重程度最高达 CVSS 9.2。这项工作发展为一项跨行业协作，以保护客户、发现变体、部署检测与缓解措施，并在协调披露前及时验证补丁。

blocks.text: 有些漏洞之所以成为转折点，是因为它们挑战了人们对安全的基本假设。2014 年，Heartbleed 暴露了保障互联网安全的共享基础设施的脆弱性。2021 年，Log4Shell 揭示了深度嵌入的软件依赖如何造成广泛暴露，而组织难以识别这些暴露。我们认为 PHP2Shell 可能标志着 AI 时代的类似转折点，说明 AI 如何改变长期存在的漏洞在实际中的可利用性。构建该漏洞利用需要串联多个缺陷，并通过反复测试和调试来适应每个目标的内存布局。前沿模型对于使这一过程变得可行至关重要，使我们能够在数小时内为多个应用开发并调整出可用的漏洞利用。随着这项工作所需的时间和专业知识减少，复杂性可能不再构成有意义的障碍，从而改变我们在实践中界定何为易受攻击的方式。

blocks.text: 所有披露的漏洞都是内存安全问题，源于 PHP 在处理请求时处理致命错误（尤其是内存不足错误）的方式中的缺陷。这些缺陷可能在请求意外结束后留下损坏的 PHP 内部状态。后续请求或工作进程可能重用该陈旧状态，导致内存泄露或损坏。

blocks.text: AI 拐点

inlines.text: AI 拐点

blocks.text: 这些存在漏洞的代码已经存在了十多年。要将这些缺陷转化为可用的漏洞利用，需要串联多个 bug，并考虑 PHP 在请求之间如何分配和复用内存。内存 bug 以复杂著称；PHP 版本、配置和应用程序行为的差异可能会打破漏洞利用所依赖的假设。针对一个部署有效的攻击，可能需要大量调整才能对另一个部署生效，每一次都需要进一步的分析、测试和调试。在 AI 出现之前，这种人工工作很难实施，更难规模化。

inlines.text: 这些存在漏洞的代码已经存在了十多年。要将这些缺陷转化为可用的漏洞利用，需要串联多个 bug，并考虑 PHP 在请求之间如何分配和复用内存。内存 bug 以复杂著称；PHP 版本、配置和应用程序行为的差异可能会打破漏洞利用所依赖的假设。针对一个部署有效的攻击，可能需要大量调整才能对另一个部署生效，每一次都需要进一步的分析、测试和调试。在 AI 出现之前，这种人工工作很难实施，更难规模化。

blocks.text: 有了 AI，这不再是障碍。LLM 可以帮助将漏洞利用适配到不同的 PHP 版本、配置和内存布局。借助测试和调试工具，模型可以分析失败并迭代调整，减少每个目标所需的专家投入。这大大降低了跨不同部署规模化攻击的门槛。

blocks.text: PHP 的 Session 模块可以在上传进度处理期间、在同一个预初始化窗口内解码会话数据。解码器将请求自有的簿记信息存储在 BG(unserialize) 中。致命的内存分配失败可能中断此路径，销毁请求堆，并使反序列化器的全局状态保持已发布状态。

blocks.text: 漏洞：远程进程内存泄露

inlines.text: 漏洞：远程进程内存泄露

blocks.text: PHP 在请求启动期间解析 RFC1867 多部分请求，此时正常模块初始化尚未完成。Session 上传进度处理可以在这个早期阶段初始化 Session 状态，并在 PS(id) 中发布会话 ID。内存不足错误可能在清理完成之前中止请求。随后 PHP 销毁请求堆，并可能使 PS(id) 指向已释放的分配。

blocks.text: 漏洞：OPcache 类型混淆

inlines.text: 漏洞：OPcache 类型混淆

blocks.text: OPcache 将编译后的 PHP 结构持久化在共享内存中，并在每个 worker 的运行时指针映射中分配索引。各 worker 通过共享 frontier 协调这些索引。在 zend_accel_script_persist() 期间，PHP 推进进程本地的 CG(map_ptr_last) frontier。只有在持久化完成后，它才会发布对应的共享 frontier。若在这两个事件之间发生分配失败，进程本地的推进就会保留下来，而部分已持久化的对象会引用共享状态仍视为可用的槽位。

blocks.text: Executive Summary

inlines.text: Executive Summary

Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others.
These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution
in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it
, putting every affected website in immediate risk.

Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.
On October 21, 2026,
PHP released the patch
fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine.

These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.

blocks.text: Overview

inlines.text: Overview

blocks.text: In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure.

That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.

blocks.text: Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.

These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption.

blocks.text: The AI inflection point

inlines.text: The AI inflection point

blocks.text: The vulnerable code had been present for more than a decade. Turning these flaws into working exploits required chaining multiple bugs and accounting for how PHP allocates and reuses memory across requests. Memory bugs are notoriously complex; differences in PHP versions, configurations and application behavior can break assumptions the exploit depends on. An attack that works against one deployment may need substantial adjustments to work against another, each requiring further analysis, testing and debugging. Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale.

blocks.text: With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments.

blocks.text: A vulnerability in core PHP reaches far beyond a single application. PHP runs across clouds, hosting providers, content-delivery networks and millions of independently managed servers. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem.

blocks.text: Technical deep dive

inlines.text: Technical deep dive

blocks.text: Bug: Upload-progress unserializer use-after-free

inlines.text: Bug: Upload-progress unserializer use-after-free

blocks.text: PHP's Session module can decode session data during upload-progress handling in the same pre-initialization window. The decoder stores request-owned bookkeeping in BG(unserialize). A fatal allocation failure can interrupt this path, destroy the request heap and leave the unserializer's global state published.

inlines.text: PHP's Session module can decode session data during upload-progress handling in the same pre-initialization window. The decoder stores request-owned bookkeeping in
BG(unserialize)
. A fatal allocation failure can interrupt this path, destroy the request heap and leave the unserializer's global state published.

blocks.text: On a later request handled by the same worker, PHP can consume attacker-reclaimed memory as live unserializer bookkeeping. The stale state becomes a powerful memory-corruption primitive. We combined it with the memory disclosure to remove address uncertainty and achieved unauthenticated remote code execution on WordPress, Drupal and Joomla.

blocks.text: The WordPress, Drupal and Joomla chains are representative demonstrations. The underlying primitives exist at the PHP engine level and can affect any PHP application running on a vulnerable version.

blocks.text: These issues execute below the application layer, so application logs may contain little context. Until systems are patched, defenders should pay particular attention to unusual multipart requests followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, and unexplained PHP worker churn. These signals can guide an investigation. Applying the PHP security update remains the only complete remediation.

blocks.text: Bug: Remote process-memory disclosure

inlines.text: Bug: Remote process-memory disclosure

blocks.text: PHP parses RFC1867 multipart requests during request startup, before normal module initialization has completed. Session upload-progress handling can initialize Session state at this early stage and publish a session ID in PS(id). An out-of-memory error can abort the request before cleanup completes. PHP then destroys the request heap and may leave PS(id) pointing to the freed allocation.

inlines.text: PHP parses RFC1867 multipart requests during request startup, before normal module initialization has completed. Session upload-progress handling can initialize Session state at this early stage and publish a session ID in
PS(id)
. An out-of-memory error can abort the request before cleanup completes. PHP then destroys the request heap and may leave
PS(id)
pointing to the freed allocation.

blocks.text: A later multipart request handled by the same worker can reach the upload-progress cleanup path before normal Session initialization resets that pointer. PHP trusts the stale pointer and length as a live zend_string and URL-encodes the reclaimed heap contents into a PHPSESSID response cookie. The attack works even when the application never calls session_start(), making the issue application-agnostic. We demonstrated unauthenticated disclosure of an attacker-sized region of live worker memory containing data from outside the attacker's request.

blocks.text: Bug: Fatal-error backtrace use-after-free

inlines.text: Bug: Fatal-error backtrace use-after-free

blocks.text: In affected versions, PHP retains the backtrace of the most recent fatal error in EG(last_fatal_error_backtrace). A fatal out-of-memory error can destroy the request heap without undefining that executor-global value. The worker survives with a global that still points to memory from the previous request.

inlines.text: In affected versions, PHP retains the backtrace of the most recent fatal error in
EG(last_fatal_error_backtrace)
. A fatal out-of-memory error can destroy the request heap without undefining that executor-global value. The worker survives with a global that still points to memory from the previous request.

blocks.text: If the same worker emits a diagnostic early in the next request, it can access the pointer before the executor reinitializes that state. PHP then destroys or updates the dangling backtrace and follows attacker-reclaimed memory. The resulting cross-request use-after-free can be developed into controlled memory corruption. We demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution against Drupal using this primitive.

blocks.text: Bug: OPcache type confusion

inlines.text: Bug: OPcache type confusion

blocks.text: OPcache persists compiled PHP structures in shared memory and assigns indices into per-worker runtime-pointer maps. Workers coordinate those indices through a shared frontier. During zend_accel_script_persist(), PHP advances the process-local CG(map_ptr_last) frontier. It publishes the corresponding shared frontier only after persistence completes. An allocation failure between those two events leaves the process-local advance in place and partially persisted objects referring to slots that the shared state still considers available.

inlines.text: OPcache persists compiled PHP structures in shared memory and assigns indices into per-worker runtime-pointer maps. Workers coordinate those indices through a shared frontier. During
zend_accel_script_persist()
, PHP advances the process-local
CG(map_ptr_last)

frontier. It publishes the corresponding shared frontier only after persistence completes. An allocation failure between those two events leaves the process-local advance in place and partially persisted objects referring to slots that the shared state still considers available.

blocks.text: When another worker later reuses one of those slots for a different runtime object, stale shared metadata resolves to a pointer of the wrong type. The mismatch creates a cross-worker type confusion and corrupts shared OPcache state. We used this primitive to build an unauthenticated RCE chain against WordPress.

blocks.text: Conclusion

inlines.text: Conclusion

blocks.text: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated. It marks an AI inflection point. The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit. With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.

blocks.text: This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. Vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. These same capabilities also give defenders a chance to uncover and fix flaws that have survived years of scrutiny.

blocks.text: Responsible disclosure timeline

inlines.text: Responsible disclosure timeline
August 19, 2026:
Wiz Research discovers the first PHP vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol.
August 20, 2026:
Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against Drupal.
August 21, 2026:
Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress.
August 24, 2026:
Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team.
September 21, 2026:
PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix.
October 21, 2026:
Patched PHP releases become available.
October 21, 2026:
Public disclosure.
